description: We’re a group of data and software engineers based in New York. The data pipeline and infrastructure are covered. We’re looking for a front-end developer, an ML engineer or data scientist, and anyone with remote sensing or wildfire knowledge.
summary: Satellites have counted fires in Argentina since 2000, but the camera changed in 2012: VIIRS sees 4 to 7 times more fire detections than MODIS, so the joined record shows a fake ×3.7 jump. Fire Calendar measures that gap month by month while both cameras flew (2012–2019), converts the older MODIS record onto the VIIRS scale, and turns the result into a burning-activity calendar from 2003 to today. Emergency managers, scientists and land managers can pick a region or draw an area and see whether a month is unusual against its own history.
details:
What it does: one consistent record of fire detections for Argentina (2003 to today) in one unit, “detections one VIIRS satellite would have counted”, shown as a month-by-year calendar coloured from much below to much above the usual month, with a likely range and a reliability flag for converted months, plus CSV download.
How it works: for each calendar month we computed the ratio of VIIRS to MODIS Aqua detections during the overlap years 2012–2019 (about 4.0 in July to 6.7 in February). Before 2012 we multiply MODIS Aqua by that month’s factor; from 2012 we use VIIRS as measured. Tested on years the method never saw (2020–2022): typical monthly error 9.5%, 9 in 10 months within 19%, and the calendar colour matched in 89% of months.
Tools: Python and DuckDB (data pipeline, Parquet), Cloudflare R2, Pages and Pages Functions (hosting and data API), HTML/CSS/JavaScript with Leaflet (web app).
Limits: tested in Argentina only; small areas before 2012 are flagged as indicative; the reference is VIIRS, not ground reports.
dataRefs: the historical MODIS and VIIRS files
